_doc: Words a Pivotal Histories line may say that a picture can show, with Wikimedia Commons search terms or categories for it (visuals.py, docs/VISUAL_BEATS_ARCHITECTURE.md §4). Used when the model pass (video/things-<n>.json) is missing; a cast entry's own name looks here too ("German horsemen" → its terms). Every picture found is still checked: a free licence, wide enough for video, and a caption built from the file's own record. Add terms as stories need them.
_context: Words that tie a Commons search result to any story of this domain, besides the story's own cast and place names (folded: accents and a plural s ignored). A search result must name its subject AND one of these or the story's names; a curated category's files need only name the subject. Empty on purpose: pivotal histories span every era, so a word like "Roman" belongs to the stories it fits, in their own stories/<slug>/video/context.json (visuals.context_words). Generic words (siege, ancient, battle) are never context: a 1799 siege of Acre is not this story.
_spoilers: Words in a picture's record that show how a story ends. A Commons picture with one is not shown before the episode that tells the ending, like the book's own pictures of it (the introduction keeps the ending back; voice.md cold open). The story's dossier `outcome.phrases` count too.
